learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the action words that follow grammar rules and the free-spirited ones that do not, by mastering finite and non-finite verbs!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Verbs are the action words or doing words that give life to a sentence! Every complete sentence needs a verb to tell us what is happening, like 'jump', 'think', or 'sleep'.
Finite verbs are the obedient rule followers. They change their form depending on the tense (Past/Present/Future) and the subject (Singular/Plural). For example, 'He PLAYS' changes to 'They PLAY'.
Non-Finite verbs are the cool rebels! They never change their spelling or form, no matter what the tense or subject is. They act like nouns or adjectives instead of main verbs.

There are three types of free birds: Infinitives (to + verb, like 'to sing'), Gerunds (verb + ing acting like a noun, like 'swimming'), and Participles (verbs acting like adjectives, like 'a broken toy').

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The Verb Detective Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Write the sentence 'I want to eat pizza.' Now change 'I' to 'She' and 'want' to the past tense. Which verb changed and which one stayed exactly the same?

quick_recap: ⭐ Finite verbs change according to the subject and the tense of the sentence.
⭐ Non-Finite verbs (Infinitives, Gerunds, and Participles) stay the same no matter what the subject or tense is!
